# Lab 8.2: SQLX Basics

## What We Are Going to Do
Declare source tables, build a view and a table with `ref()`, run them, and look at the dependency graph.

## Steps

1. **[Console] Declare the sources.** In the workspace, create `definitions/sources/thelook.sqlx`:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">config {
  type: "declaration",
  database: "bigquery-public-data",
  schema: "thelook_ecommerce",
  name: "orders"
}</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Create a second file `definitions/sources/users.sqlx` the same way with `name: "users"`.

2. **[Console] Build a staging view.** Create `definitions/staging/stg_orders.sqlx`:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">config {
  type: "view",
  description: "Cleaned orders"
}

SELECT order_id, user_id, LOWER(status) AS status, created_at, num_of_item
FROM ${ref("orders")}
WHERE created_at IS NOT NULL</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[Console] Build a mart table.** Create `definitions/marts/orders_by_country.sqlx`:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">config {
  type: "table",
  description: "Orders per country and status",
  bigquery: { partitionBy: "order_month", clusterBy: ["country"] }
}

SELECT u.country, o.status, DATE_TRUNC(DATE(o.created_at), MONTH) AS order_month, COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM ${ref("stg_orders")} o
JOIN ${ref("users")} u ON o.user_id = u.id
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[Console] Compile and look at the graph.** Click **Compiled graph**. You see `orders` and `users` → `stg_orders` → `orders_by_country`. Click any node to see the compiled SQL.

5. **[Console] Run it.** Click **Start execution → All actions → Start execution**. Open **Executions** to watch it.

6. **[CLI] Check the outputs.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq ls lab08
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false 'SELECT * FROM lab08.orders_by_country ORDER BY orders DESC LIMIT 5'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Declarations | Public tables usable with `ref()` |
| `ref()` | Builds the dependency order |
| Outputs | View `stg_orders`, table `orders_by_country` |
| Graph | Sources → staging → mart |
